title: The five responses, one at a time
lede: What each response can sound like, what the person may need, and the well-meant reply that shuts the conversation down.
intent: Learners can describe what each response can sound like, what the person may need, and what not to say.
goal: describe what each response can sound like, what the person may need, and what not to say.
intro: Three columns: what you might hear, what the person may need, and what not to say. The rows fill in one at a time. The order of the rows is the order Kübler-Ross listed them in, and nothing more.

items.label: What it can sound like
values: There has been a mistake. Get the tests done again.
Why did nobody pick this up sooner? Often aimed at whoever is in the room.
If I do everything right, will that change it? Often carries what if and if only.
Little talk. Withdrawal from things that used to matter.
I want to get the house sorted out. Practical planning.

items.label: What the person may need
values: Time, and the information offered again later rather than pressed now.
To be heard without the anger being taken personally or argued down.
Honesty about what is and is not possible, given without stripping out hope.
Someone present rather than fixing it. Watch for risk and escalate to a supervisor.
Support to act on the decisions they have made themselves.

items.label: What not to say
values: There is no point getting angry about it.
That is not going to make any difference.
Try to look on the bright side.
You are being so brave about it.

steps.say: Denial. The information itself is pushed away. What helps is time: offer it again later rather than pressing it now.
Anger. Often aimed at whoever is in the room, which on placement may be you. It is rarely about you, so let it be heard rather than defending anyone.
Bargaining. If I do this, then that, or if only. It sounds hopeful and practical, which is why it is easy to miss. Be honest without taking the hope away.
Depression. Withdrawal and loss of meaning. Be present rather than trying to fix it, and this is the one where you watch for risk and tell your supervisor.
Acceptance. Not happiness, but planning around what is real. Support the person to act on their own decisions. And remember: these five can come in any order, and come back.

teach.watchFor: The room reading the rows as a sequence. Say out loud, at the first and last step, that the order is only the order they were listed in.

sources.label: Kübler-Ross, E. (1969). On Death and Dying.
Replies and needs written for this activity
sources.note: Check against your service's communication guidance.
